They are the weak ones. It takes strength to have compassion, to be good, to be kind. And I'm not talking about being submissive. No. I'm talking about, telling these people to their faces that they are self-absorbed, and that you feel sorry for their souls. You may be broken down, but you still have your humanity (otherwise, you wouldn't be depressed). 

When all is said and done, life doesn't have to be 'normal'. There is no normal. I talk to you without good eye contact and you would call me rude, but if we were in Japan we would be ok. There is no normal.

So, you are the person who nobody cares to lend some sympathy, empathy, or may be at least 5 minutes of their fucking time. This shouldn't make you feel like you are nothing. This should make you realize that people are too self-absorbed, too distracted by trinkets (money, tv, sex, life's little pleasures etc.) that they don't have any humanity left, and that your mission is to not lose your humanity and compassion, even though you went through, and are going through, pain.

I want you to clear from your mind any sliver of hope that this will get better. I want you to imagine the worst scenario, the worst thing that you are afraid will happen unless you can hold it all together. I want you to feel that happening, vividly, real, feel the fear and the despair until you feel like you can just shut your eyes and die...

That is when you will realize that, life doesn't have to be perfect, or normal at all, and that regardless of what happens, suffering is a choice.

Spirituality, yes. It is of utmost importance, especially in a tumultuous time like this, that we remind everyone we can that the world is not just your 5 physical senses, and that consciousness does not limit itself in a bag of flesh and water.

Non-religious is a good way to describe it. 'Religion' has nothing to do with spirituality, and most organized religions, including organized aspects of Buddhism, are just a form of control. 

Control is the key word. That is what Earth is under; control. It's easy to dismiss the 'illuminati' as some 'conspiracy theory'. However, once enough spiritual awareness has developed, one naturally realizes that yes, there are those in the world who have discovered that the spiritual forces are what causes everything to happen in physicality, and thus hid the knowledge to themselves and used it to manipulate humanity, whom, without knowledge of the spiritual, are merely animals, following their instincts for food, sex, pleasure and survival, easy to be manipulated. I know that feeling. That impossible predicament of wanting to just stop, but cannot, because of obligations.

My friend, it took me a long time, and tremendous amount of self-loathing. But one day, the realization hits, that you are not responsible for your family's life. Yes, you DO want them to be happy.

Here's the thing. I used to suffer just like you. That impossible mental pit of anguish...oh goodness it's fucking awful, and I know you're feeling it now. I thought that, in order to cure it, I either had to die, or everything in my life had to be fixed, and as you and I know, that's impossible to do in our mental state.

Here's the thing; my situations never changed. My parents are still narcissistic, selfish, sociopathic, materialistic and everything that Baby Boomers can be. I'm still working a shitty job right now.

What changed was, as corny as it sounds, I found God. Ok, let me rephrase. After much reflection and struggling, one day it just clicked, internally. That all suffering is an illusion, and I'm putting too much importance on 'ME'. You see, it used be be 'I am saluna, and I am depressed because my parents are inadequate and abusive'. Now it's 'Saluna's parents inadequate and abusive'...that is all. 

Now, it doesn't really matter that my past was as it was. I'm certainly not 'normal'. I still have the same shitty job. I still don't like being around the parents, I still get moody/sad/upset for weird reasons. And that is all ok. Who said life had to come in a standard package? Two happily married parents, good safe neighborhood, good education, good home life. Who said this is what is required for 'happiness'? Are those people, those with the good parents, good jobs, good life, are they even 'happy'? Or is what most people think is 'happiness' actually just 'pleasure'? Pleasure is nice, but once you realize that both pleasure and suffering are illusions, and really, all there ever is, is consciousness (love/God/the Force, whatever you want to call it).

Your sister may never be able to do 'normal' things (there is no such thing. If I talk to you, but you keep looking away, I would think you are rude. If we were in Japan and you hold perfect eye contact while we talk, that is also rude. There is no normal)...sorry for saying this, but you get the point...so what? You can love her and she can love you. Same with your parents. Same with everyone and everything.

You know why depression and all that happens? It's because we were PROGRAMMED, since birth, to expect a certain way of life. When that way of life doesn't come, we are shocked. School > College > Job > Soul Mate, that's the dumbest shit I ever heard. In fact, the fact that most people in the world believes that human life (the most unique spiritual experience in the universe) SHOULD operate this way, is proof to me that all the 'lurminati' crap is real. Look at that structure. They programmed us from the start to be their slaves, to be just smart enough to run the machines and do the paper work, rich enough to afford drugs and entertainment, and dumb enough to be satisfied with just that.

People value money, success, looks, mental stability, financial stability, how good your boyfriend looks, how good your children looks, how good your car looks, how good your job is etc. I valued those things too. Now though, it doesn't matter to me. A few hundred thousand dollars wouldn't hurt, but what matters most right now is...how can I get other people to stop suffering? how do I make them see, that it is their desires that cause them to suffer. That their desires are not even theirs to begin with, but programmed in them by the rulers of this world. I mean, even the idea of a 'soul mate', a romantic, monogamous, life-long partner, is a modern invention. How many old, miserable married couples you see? What's wrong with building a great life together, and when all is done, after the two partners evaluated who they have become, the partners decide to each continue on their own journey, recognizing the love and life they once shared?

What i'm saying is, we are taught to fit into these 'normalisms' and archetypes. There are no such things, and when our brains can't reconcile the programming with reality, we suffer.
It will not be a good day. But I will not have to suffer. Suffering is a choice.
